_comment: Committed metric baselines for the rb-eval regression gate. The harness FAILS if a quality metric drops below its baseline (with a 1e-9 tolerance). These were captured from a run over the committed fixtures with DeterministicProvider and reproduce bit-for-bit across runs. They guard ranking DETERMINISM and RELATIVE ORDERING (regression detection), not absolute semantic quality; see README.md. History: the W1.0a corpus expansion (12 -> 205 memories, 10 -> 72 natural-language goldens) reset recall@k to 0.0486 / mrr to 0.0518 -- the honest pre-Phase-1 starting line. W1.1+W1.7 (cosine metric + namespace partition) left recall@k unchanged and moved mrr to 0.0505 (noise-tie reshuffle). Re-captured for W1.2 (FTS tokenization): the keyword leg is ALIVE for natural-language queries (OR-of-individually-quoted-tokens replaces the whole-query phrase; porter stemming layered over unicode61 via migration 005), so the deterministic gate metrics jumped: recall@k 0.0486 -> 0.7847, mrr 0.0505 -> 0.9611 -- under non-semantic deterministic vectors the FTS channel is now the dominant useful signal, which is exactly the channel W1.2 revived (fts_query_rate 0.042 -> 1.0). dedup_precision moved 1.0 -> 0.9917: improved retrieval now co-ranks both members of some expected near-dup clusters in top-5, the legitimate trade the previous comment anticipated. The REAL-vector replay measurement vs docs/eval/2026-06-12-pre-phase1-baseline.json: golden recall@5 0.9213 -> 0.9630, mrr 0.9838 -> 0.9838 (flat), ndcg 0.9342 -> 0.9537, dedup 0.9306 -> 0.9472, fts_query_rate 0.0417 -> 1.0 (Phase 1 gate: >= 0.80). Versus the intermediate post-W1.1 state, replay mrr traded 0.9931 -> 0.9838 and ndcg 0.9558 -> 0.9537 for the recall/dedup/channel gains (full variant table in the escape_fts5_query decision record and the W1.2 commit body). Raising a baseline after an intentional ranking improvement, or lowering one for a justified trade-off, is a deliberate reviewed commit. Latency p50/p99 are reported but not gated (machine-dependent). Re-verified for W1.3 (score floor + empty state): the Linear recall floor SCORE_FLOOR=0.18 moved NO metric in any context -- deterministic gate recall@k/mrr/dedup bit-identical (the gate corpus is all-fresh, imp >= 5, so every returned result already scores >= 0.2253), and real-vector replay goldens (0.9630/0.9838/0.9537/0.9472) are bit-identical with the floor on vs off -- the floor only trims below-floor tail junk (positions past the metric horizon). Derivation arithmetic lives on rb_search::SCORE_FLOOR; the sweep tool is rb-eval/tests/score_floor_diag.rs. Re-captured for W1.4 (query-kind embeddings): NO metric moved -- DeterministicProvider is kind-blind by design (embed_query == embed_document, pinned by test), so the deterministic gate is bit-identical (0.7847/0.9611/0.9917), and the committed all-MiniLM-L6-v2 replay fixture serves query-kind lookups via the document-kind fallback (byte-identical vectors for this kind-blind model), so replay goldens (0.9630/0.9838/0.9537/0.9472) are bit-identical too. The semantic effect of input_type=query lands only when a Voyage fixture is recorded (key required; deferred). Re-captured for W1.5 (real graph hops): NO metric moved -- bit-identical deterministic gate (0.7847/0.9611/0.9917) AND bit-identical real-vector replay (goldens 0.9630/0.9838/0.9537/0.9472, all 72 golden per-query rankings unchanged at full precision). Why: recall expands the graph at depth 1, so every graph-surfaced candidate is a DIRECT neighbor; the chosen 1/hops decay gives a 1-hop neighbor the full graph weight, exactly what the old index-as-hops scheme incidentally awarded the (typically single) first-listed neighbor -- so scores coincide wherever the old behavior was right, and the fix only bites multi-neighbor lists (old: second-listed direct neighbor halved) and future depth>1 walks, neither of which this corpus's sparse linker-generated graph (graph_query_rate 0.028 golden / 0.10 holdout) exercises into a rank flip. NDCG GATED (Phase-1 review pass): ndcg over the authored per-query grades joins the gated quality metrics at its current deterministic value, so a grade-ordering regression that keeps the binary metrics intact (a grade-3 primary answer swapping ranks with a grade-1 marginal one inside top-5) fails CI instead of passing silently; no ranking semantics changed -- this is a new gate on an already-reported metric. HOLDOUT POLICY (Phase-1 review pass): the held-out query set's aggregates are measured ONLY at frozen-artifact captures (examples/capture_baseline.rs) and by the future W4.1 CI gate -- NEVER in per-workstream verification, automated or human. Earlier W1.3-W1.5 notes in this comment cited holdout aggregates per ranking change; those citations were removed (they survive in branch commit history, written before this rule was adopted) because checking holdout deltas after each tuning decision is itself an optimization loop that erodes the set's held-out status before W4.1 gates on it. The default test suite no longer runs the holdout queries (rb-eval/tests/replay_model.rs holdout replay is #[ignore]d). Re-verified after the eval clock pin (Phase-2 flake fix): the engine's with_fixed_now hook stamps every corpus row AND ranking-now at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, so (now - created_at) is exactly zero for all memories instead of riding insert/query wall-clock timing -- this removes the rrf_mode_is_deterministic_across_runs flake class (near-tied RRF ranks flipping when the suite ran slowly enough for recency priors to drift between the two runs). NO metric moved: deterministic gate bit-identical (0.7847/0.9611/0.9917/0.8514) -- the corpus was already all-fresh so priors were ~1.0; they are now exactly 1.0.
